content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built a limitation-by-limitation source ledger against the disclosure and the USER passage in the conversation.

**Ledger result (summary of tracing):** every claim limitation in claims 1–17, every one of the 30 ledger numerals, and every structure, relationship, flow path, material state, and optional feature in the description and figure briefs traces to an affirmative sentence in `input/disclosure.md`. Spot checks of the highest-risk items:

- Claim 1's whereby-clause circulation path → "Warm air rising from the product region enters the central inlet, divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts, enters the side supply passages, passes through perforations in the product tray, and returns through the lower return passage."
- Claims 2/13 sequencing (register, then seal) → "A compressible lid gasket seals against the upper edge of the shell **after registration**."
- Claims 3/14 → "presses resilient feet of the spacer frame against ledges of the shell so that the module cannot lift away from the tray during transport."
- Claims 6–8, 16 → the wick/condensate-channel/pull-tab paragraph verbatim.
- Claims 9–11, 17 → the indicator paragraph, including "does not control airflow."
- Optional-feature framing in **Variations** → "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features."

**Functional-surface geometry check (the v10 focus):** the briefs stay minimal on the mating channel (no depth, taper, lead-in, or which-end statements), the ledge/resilient-foot joint, the gasket/upper-edge seal, and the duct ports. Which-end statements that do appear — outlet opening and condensate opening "at the lower end of the duct," inlet "open downward toward the tray" — are compelled by the disclosed flow sequence and by "Openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts." No "by way of example," "any closed outline," or renderer-justifying embodiment language appears in the application text.

No unsupported technical assertion was found. Three verified internal-consistency/formalities defects are reported below.

input.summary: Full preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all seventeen claims (device claims 1-11, conditioning method 12-15, servicing method 16-17), all thirty entries of the numeral ledger and each numbered part's use in the description and in every figure brief, all six figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings, and each specific structure, relationship, flow path, operating condition, and optional variant in the summary and detailed description, back to affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md (the conversation.md USER passage is a truncated duplicate of the same text and adds nothing). Every substantive item is supported: the four-body carrier, tray feet and lower return passage, inward-spaced tray walls and two side supply passages, the rigid spacer frame with central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the opposed cassettes and peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages, the full closed circulation sequence, the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" limitation, the depending indexing rib / mating channel registration and the register-then-seal ordering of the compressible lid gasket, the resilient feet pressed against shell ledges, the wick / shallow condensate channel / condensate discharge openings / pull tab, and the mechanical exposure indicator with stem, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, manual-reset-only behaviour and "does not control airflow." The optional framing in the Variations section traces to "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features." Applying the functional-surface-geometry test, I checked the mating channel, the ledge/resilient-foot joint, the gasket-to-upper-edge seal, the inlet, the duct ports and the indicator bore for undisclosed depth, which-end, taper, angle, runout or contact-topology statements: the which-end statements that appear (outlet and condensate openings at the lower end of the duct, inlet open downward toward the tray, duct upper end open to the dividing space) are compelled by the disclosed flow sequence and by "Openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel," and the remaining outlines (rectangular shell, slab lid, schematic indicator housing, closed-loop gasket band) are declared schematic, add no technical function, and are not verbalized in the application text. No "by way of example," "any closed outline," or other renderer-justifying embodiment statement appears in the filed text, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative remains in sections 01-10 or in numerals.md. Section line 2-2 carries the same repeated designation in the FIG. 1 source brief, the FIG. 2 view brief, and the Brief Description; the four unnumbered broken circles in FIG. 2 map one-to-one and by consistent position wording to FIGS. 3-6. No unsupported technical assertion was found. Three verified defects are reported, all internal-consistency or formalities: FIG. 1's brief cites numeral 52 in prose although its own numeral list (correctly) omits it, creating a leader risk; FIG. 4 describes the side supply passage as "outboard of and below" the peripheral outlet opening while the same brief and the disclosure require the opening to overlap that passage; and FIG. 6 contains a doubled sentence-terminal period.

findings.title: FIG. 1 brief cites numeral 52 in prose although the figure's numeral list omits it
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, module 40 bullet and the "Numerals shown on this figure" list
findings.detail: The FIG. 1 brief names reference numeral 52 in its prose while expressly stating that the recess is unnumbered, and the figure's own numeral list correctly omits 52. Every other brief keeps prose numerals and the numeral list in exact agreement (FIG. 2, for example, refers to "the mechanical exposure indicator" with no numeral because 80 is not on that sheet). The mismatch invites the renderer to letter and leader a 52 onto FIG. 1, which would then conflict with the numeral list, with FIG. 3 (the only view where 52 is shown), and with the Detailed Description, which introduces the mating channel 52 in connection with FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 but relies on FIG. 3 for its depiction.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-1.md: "an unnumbered upwardly open recess, corresponding to the mating channel 52, is formed in its upper surface" — but the same file lists only "- 10 / - 16 / - 20 / - 26 / - 40 / - 60 / - 62 / - 64" under "## Numerals shown on this figure".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, replace "an unnumbered upwardly open recess, corresponding to the mating channel 52, is formed in its upper surface" with "an unnumbered upwardly open recess, which receives the depending indexing rib 62 when the lid 60 is closed, is formed in its upper surface". Leave the numeral list unchanged.

findings.title: FIG. 4 places the side supply passage "outboard of" the peripheral outlet opening while also requiring the two to overlap
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, "Side supply passage 30" bullet, read against the "Peripheral outlet opening 50" bullet and the closing statement in the same brief
findings.detail: Within a single brief the side supply passage 30 is located outboard of the peripheral outlet opening 50, yet the same brief twice states that opening 50 overlaps that passage. A passage that lies outboard of the opening is laterally offset from it and cannot overlap it, so the two statements cannot both be rendered. The overlap is the disclosed registration relationship and must govern; the word "outboard" is the untraced addition. The word "below" alone is accurate and consistent with FIG. 2, which shows the passages "open at the top" beneath the gap in the periphery of the module.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-4.md: "Side supply passage 30: a blank open upright space outboard of and below the peripheral outlet opening 50" versus, in the same file, "the opening 50 overlapping that passage, shown schematically" and "the opening 50 overlapping the upper end of that passage so that the two are in open communication". Source: disclosure.md, "peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages" and "a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, change "a blank open upright space outboard of and below the peripheral outlet opening 50" to "a blank open upright space below the peripheral outlet opening 50". Make no other change to the bullet.

findings.title: Doubled sentence-terminal period in the FIG. 6 brief
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md, "Mechanical exposure indicator 80" bullet, final characters
findings.detail: The indicator bullet ends with two consecutive full stops. This is a typographical defect in a delivered drawing specification and should be corrected before the brief is frozen for rendering.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-6.md: "the indicator 80 is shown in the retained condition, the stem 82 not yet having been moved by the spring 86 to the latched exposed position.."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-6.md, replace "to the latched exposed position.." with "to the latched exposed position."
